## [2026-05-24] ingest | DSPy Tutorial — Caching
- **Source**: `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/cache/` — short single-page [[DSPy]] tutorial canonicalizing the framework's caching surface. Raw saved at `raw/dspy-cache-tutorial.md`; source page at `wiki/sources/dspy-cache-tutorial.md`.
- **Position in the corpus**: **Thirteenth wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial** and the **third "production-shape, programming-stage-only" tutorial** in the corpus alongside [[dspy-async-tutorial]] and [[dspy-streaming-tutorial]] — these three canonicalize **async / streaming / caching** as orthogonal production-shape axes over [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the four-concerns decomposition]]. No metric, no optimizer, no dataset.
- **Load-bearing additions to the corpus**:
  1. **Three-layer caching taxonomy** — *in-memory* ([[LRUCache]] via `cachetools.LRUCache`) + *on-disk* (`diskcache.FanoutCache`) + *provider-side* ([[PromptCaching]] managed by [[anthropic|Anthropic]] / [[openai|OpenAI]]). First two are **on by default**; the third is opt-in via `cache_control_injection_points=[{"location": "message", "role": "system"}]` on [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM(...)`]]. First wiki receipt of the `(memory, disk, provider)` triple as a single framework-level taxonomy.
  2. **`dspy.configure_cache` is the single configuration surface** — six parameters: `enable_disk_cache` / `enable_memory_cache` (layer toggles), `disk_size_limit_bytes` / `memory_max_entries` (capacity), `restrict_pickle` / `safe_types` (security). First wiki receipt of every parameter.
  3. **`dspy.clients.Cache` subclassing is the custom-key escape hatch** — override `cache_key()` / `get()` / `put()`, then assign `dspy.cache = CustomCache(...)`. Canonical example hashes `sha256(orjson.dumps(messages, option=orjson.OPT_SORT_KEYS))` to ignore model selection so semantically-equivalent prompts share cache hits **across [[DSPyLM|LM]] versions** — demonstrated by switching from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` to `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` under `dspy.context(...)` and observing a cache hit instead of the default miss.
- **Three operational disclosures across the cache ↔ rest-of-DSPy boundary**:
  1. **Default `cache_key` hashes all litellm request args except credentials** — the model name is part of the key, so switching models misses by default under the stock cache. The custom-cache example above is the canonical workaround.
  2. **Cached responses return `None` for `result.get_lm_usage()` under [[DSPyLM|`track_usage=True`]]** — no provider call occurred. This closes the usage-tracking ↔ caching interaction left implicit by prior [[DSPyLM]] / [[DSPyPredict]] receipts.
  3. **Streaming is disabled by cache hit** (from [[dspy-streaming-tutorial]]) — only the final [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]] arrives when the [[DSPyLM|LM]] call is cached. This tutorial documents the **reverse direction** of the same interaction: when caching is on, streaming silently collapses; when streaming is wanted, the multi-field example must use `dspy.LM(..., cache=False)` deliberately. The cache/streaming/usage triad is now closed end-to-end across the corpus.
- **Security disclosure — `restrict_pickle`**:
  - `restrict_pickle=True` swaps in an **allowlist-based deserializer**. Default allowlist: LiteLLM and OpenAI response types (pydantic models for LM calls, embeddings, Responses API) + NumPy array reconstruction helpers (for embedding caches) + user types via `safe_types=[...]`.
  - **Unapproved types degrade to a cache miss with a log entry, not a raised exception** — graceful-degradation discipline. The cache returns `None` and logs the rejected type; the program proceeds to a fresh provider call.
  - Nested custom types must each be registered separately in `safe_types`.
  - **Why it matters**: without restriction, a tampered on-disk cache file could trigger arbitrary code execution during unpickling. Critical when the cache directory is shared, synced, or otherwise reachable by untrusted parties — e.g., shared dev environments, [[DataLineage|build artifacts]], CI caches.
- **Composition with prior tutorials**:
  - [[dspy-async-tutorial]]: caching applies uniformly to `acall` / `aforward`-routed programs — async DSPy hits the same memory + disk + provider layers as sync DSPy. No special async cache configuration.
  - [[dspy-streaming-tutorial]]: streaming + caching are **mutually-exclusive at the per-call level** — the cache hit short-circuits the sidecar token stream. The streaming tutorial's `cache=False` workaround is the canonical pattern for "I want to see the tokens this time."
  - [[dspy-optimizer-tracking-tutorial]] / [[MIPROv2]] / [[GEPA]]: long optimizer runs benefit **massively** from the disk cache — the optimizer issues hundreds-to-thousands of LM calls during search; the disk cache turns a re-run into a near-zero-cost replay. The on-disk layer's `disk_size_limit_bytes` parameter becomes load-bearing for multi-experiment optimization workflows.
  - [[DSPyEvaluation]]: cached eval reruns distort latency numbers — the tutorial's use-case list calls out **disable caching for benchmarking** as one of the eight named scenarios.
  - [[dspy-customer-service-agent]] / [[dspy-mem0-react-tutorial]] / [[dspy-yahoo-finance-react-tutorial]]: ReAct loops are the **headline use case** for provider-side prompt caching — long static tool schemas + few-shot demos repeat on every iteration, so `cache_control_injection_points` on the system message is the production-shape recommendation.
- **Concept / entity updates**: **mints 1 new concept page** — [[DSPyCache]] (canonical framework-wide caching pattern; orthogonal to [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the four-concerns decomposition]]; cross-links to [[LRUCache]] / [[PromptCaching]] / [[DSPyLM]] / [[DSPyAsync]] / [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[DSPyOptimization]]). No entity pages minted — [[anthropic|Anthropic]] / [[openai|OpenAI]] are referenced as existing provider-side prompt-cache hosts; no new providers.
- **Index updates**: Sources entry inserted in the DSPy-tutorial block adjacent to [[dspy-customer-service-agent]] (the chronological sibling — both are end-DSPy-block tutorials). Concepts entry [[DSPyCache]] inserted in the Concepts block above [[DSPyData]] (alphabetical within the `DSPy*` cluster).
- **No contradictions** with prior wiki content. The tutorial **extends** every prior DSPy ingest along an orthogonal caching axis. Specific reconciliations:
  - The wiki's existing [[PromptCaching]] concept (provider-generic) is now anchored to a concrete DSPy framework surface (`cache_control_injection_points`) — the page moves from "concept-only" to "concept + framework binding".
  - The wiki's existing [[LRUCache]] page (generic eviction strategy) is now anchored to its concrete role as DSPy's in-memory layer implementation.
  - The wiki's existing [[CachePolicy]] / cache-coherency cluster from the [[dis-11-4-caching|systems caching]] line is **distinct** from this application-layer cache — no risk of conflation; the systems pages cover hardware/OS caches, this page covers LM-request caching at the framework layer.
- **Productive clarifications**:
  1. **DSPy caching is on by default.** Users running `dspy.Predict` against the same prompt twice will see the second call return instantly with `None` usage — this is the expected behavior, not a bug. Disable both layers via `dspy.configure_cache(enable_disk_cache=False, enable_memory_cache=False)` if fresh responses are required every run.
  2. **The default cache key includes the model name.** Cross-model cache hits require a custom `cache_key`. This is the framework's safe default — different models can return materially different outputs for identical prompts; sharing hits is an explicit user choice via subclassing.
  3. **Provider-side prompt caching is opt-in, not free.** The user must add `cache_control_injection_points` to `dspy.LM(...)` — DSPy does not auto-enable provider-side caching even when the in-memory and on-disk layers are both on. The three layers are independent.
  4. **`restrict_pickle` should be the default for any shared cache directory.** The tutorial does not call this out, but the security implications are clear: if the cache directory is on a shared filesystem or is checked into version control, `restrict_pickle=True` is mandatory, not optional.

Not specified; (7) no concurrent-write guidance — what happens when two processes write to the same `disk_cache_dir` simultaneously? `diskcache.FanoutCache` handles this safely but the tutorial doesn't say so; (8) no benchmark of the in-memory LRU eviction surface — `memory_max_entries` default value is not stated.

Distinct from `acall` because asyncify runs the **sync** inner program on a **thread pool** (sized by `dspy.configure(async_max_workers=N)`, default 8), whereas `acall` requires the program to be natively async. - **Productive clarifications**:
  1. **`asyncify` is not `acall`.** Both produce awaitable callables, but `asyncify` runs the **sync** inner program on a **thread pool** while `acall` requires the program to be **natively async** (event-loop dispatch). Choosing between them is a code-shape decision (sync vs async program) not a performance decision; both unblock the event loop, but asyncify pays the thread-pool cost.
  2. **`async_max_workers=N` is the asyncify capacity knob.** Default 8; tuning trades concurrent-request capacity against memory pressure and LM-provider rate-limit thrashing. Distinct from the (non-existent) thread-pool size for `acall` (no pool — pure event loop).

- **Source**: `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/observability/` — short single-page [[DSPy]] tutorial; **canonicalizes the three-tier observability stack** of the framework. Wiki page: `wiki/sources/dspy-observability-tutorial.md`.
- **Three-tier stack**:
  1. **Tier 1 — `dspy.inspect_history(n=N)`** ([[InspectHistory]]): zero-dep print of last *N* LM calls. Three documented limitations motivate the upgrade: LM-only (no [[DSPyTools|tool]] / retriever / [[DSPyAdapters|adapter]] coverage), no metadata (latency / module relationships), ambiguous ordering under nested predictions.
  2. **Tier 2 — [[MLflow]] autolog**: `mlflow server --backend-store-uri sqlite:///mydb.sqlite` + `mlflow.set_tracking_uri(...)` + `mlflow.set_experiment("DSPy")` + `mlflow.autolog()`. Captures *"DSPy modules, LM calls, retriever invocations, and tool executions"* automatically.
  3. **Tier 3 — `BaseCallback`** ([[DSPyCallback]]): user-programmable instrumentation. Six start/end handler pairs (`on_module_*`, `on_lm_*`, `on_adapter_format_*`, `on_adapter_parse_*`, `on_tool_*`, `on_evaluate_*`). Registered via `dspy.configure(callbacks=[...])`.
- **First wiki receipts**:
  - **`dspy.utils.callback.BaseCallback`** — framework's user-programmable instrumentation interface. Six handler pairs documented in [[DSPyCallback]]; signatures `*_start(call_id, instance, inputs)` / `*_end(call_id, outputs, exception)`; `call_id` pairs start with end for nested calls; `exception=None` on success.
  - **Unscoped `mlflow.autolog()` form** for DSPy autotracing — vs the kwarg-bearing `mlflow.dspy.autolog(...)` form in [[dspy-custom-module]] / [[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent]] / [[dspy-optimizer-tracking-tutorial]]. Both invocations route to the same DSPy integration; the scoped form is the canonical surface for compile-time kwargs (`log_compiles` / `log_evals` / `log_traces_from_compile`).
  - **`mlflow>=2.18.0`** — lowest MLflow floor in the DSPy tutorial corpus. Beneath the `mlflow>=2.21.1` floor in [[dspy-optimizer-tracking-tutorial]] and the `mlflow>=3.0.0` floor in [[dspy-custom-module]]. Inference-time DSPy autologging is supported on the MLflow 2.x line from 2.18 forward.
  - **Selective callback filtering by Signature name** — the tutorial's `AgentLoggingCallback` checks `instance.signature.__name__` and logs only [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]]'s reasoning steps (those with `Thought*` output keys), demonstrating the tier-3 advantage over tier 2 (`mlflow.autolog()` has no equivalent filter).
- **Canonical retrieval-staleness diagnosis pattern**: the tutorial's load-bearing demonstration uses a [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] agent over the [[ColBERTv2]] public Wikipedia endpoint to answer *"Which baseball team does Shohei Ohtani play for?"*. The agent returns the **stale** answer ("Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters" — Ohtani's pre-2018 team), invisible at the LM-output layer (chain-of-thought looks well-grounded) and only visible by **hovering the retriever span in the MLflow trace UI** to read the returned article directly. Fix: substitute a [[Tavily]] web-search [[DSPyTools|`dspy.Tool`]] — no other program changes — corrected answer confirmed via the same trace UI. Receipt for the framing thesis *"Without transparency, the prediction process can easily become a black box."*

- **Files created**: `raw/dspy-output-refinement-tutorial.md`, `wiki/sources/dspy-output-refinement-tutorial.md`, `wiki/concepts/DSPyBestOfN.md`, `wiki/concepts/DSPyRefine.md`.

- **Headline contribution**: **migration receipt** — DSPy 2.6 replaces [[DSPyAssert|`dspy.Assert`]] / [[DSPySuggest|`dspy.Suggest`]] (the boolean-constraint API from [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]]) with [[DSPyBestOfN|`dspy.BestOfN`]] / [[DSPyRefine|`dspy.Refine`]] (a scalar-reward API). Boolean `constraint` → `reward_fn(args, pred) -> float`; binary halt/warn → `fail_count` for halt + `Refine`-vs-`BestOfN` for feedback-vs-no-feedback. The retry-with-feedback semantics from [[AssertionDrivenBacktracking|backtracking]] survive in `Refine` but with framework-synthesized feedback in place of user-authored `msg`.
- **API surface canonicalized**: `dspy.BestOfN(module, N, reward_fn, threshold, fail_count=None)` and `dspy.Refine(module, N, reward_fn, threshold, fail_count=None)` — identical four-kwarg surfaces; difference is the auto-feedback-loop step `Refine` inserts between rollouts.
- **Cache interaction**: rollout-ID variation is the cache-bypass mechanism — first wiki receipt of an *intentional* cache miss, inverse of the [[dspy-cache-tutorial|caching tutorial's]] hit-path optimization.
- **Worked examples** (3): one-word-answer constraint (`N=3`, threshold=1.0, shared verbatim between both modules to highlight API symmetry); `FactualityJudge`-driven refinement (LM-as-judge `is_factual: bool` Signature composed inside `reward_fn`); length-controlled summarization (`BestOfN(N=50, threshold=0.9)` with tapering `1.0 - distance/125` around 75-word target).
- **Distinguishing properties** vs the generic [[bestofn|Best-of-N]] test-time-scaling pattern: programmable `reward_fn` (vs majority-vote / [[Logprobs|logprob]] aggregation); threshold-based early-exit (vs full-N-then-aggregate); `fail_count` error-tolerance baked into selection (vs abort-on-error).
- **Lineage**: `Refine` inherits the *"re-invoke failing module with prior erring output + msg injected as `Past Query` / `Instruction` prompt fields"* mechanism from [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]] §3 ([[AssertionDrivenBacktracking]]); only the API shape changed — boolean constraint with user-authored `msg` became scalar `reward_fn` with framework-synthesized feedback.
- **Contradiction with prior corpus**: [[DSPyAssert]] / [[DSPySuggest]] were the documented active API in the wiki. **Reconciled**: both pages keep their original API documentation for historical reference and as the source for the [[AssertionDrivenBacktracking]] / [[AssertionDrivenExampleBootstrapping]] / [[CounterexampleBootstrapping]] compile-time machinery; deprecation banner at the top of each points readers to the new modules.

Diff is **MCP packaging** — tools are now decorated with `@mcp.tool()` and served from a separate process instead of being passed as plain Python callables to `dspy.ReAct(..., tools=[fn1, fn2, ...])`. Confirms [[DSPyMCP|the binding's]] *"MCP-converted tools are indistinguishable from local-function tools after conversion"* claim with a side-by-side experimental control.
- **Entity minted**: [[FastMCP]] — `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP`, the decorator-style Python helper for authoring MCP servers (part of [[anthropic|Anthropic]]'s official Python MCP SDK). Three-line scaffolding (`mcp = FastMCP("Name")` + `@mcp.tool()` per function + `mcp.run()`); auto-derives JSON Schema from type hints (including [[Pydantic]] models). Pairs with the previously-documented client-side [[DSPyMCP|`dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`]].
- **Subpatterns named** (2): (1) **deterministic-utility tool** — the tutorial's `pick_flight(flights: list[Flight])` is internal Python (sort by `(duration, price)`) exposed as a tool, pushing ordering / comparison / tie-breaking out of the LM and into deterministic code; (2) **LM-friendly type design** — *"Somehow LLM is bad at specifying `datetime.datetime`"* (inline comment on the custom `Date(year, month, day, hour)` Pydantic model) justifies integer-field BaseModels over ISO-8601 strings the LM tends to mis-emit.
- **First-of-kind receipt**: serialization-boundary defensive coding. The `pick_flight` body uses `x.get('duration') if isinstance(x, dict) else x.duration` to accommodate the JSON-wire downgrade from [[Pydantic]] `BaseModel` to plain `dict`. Prior wiki DSPy receipts passed Pydantic objects between functions where class binding survived; MCP introduces a JSON wire boundary that the tool author must accommodate.
- **First-of-kind callout**: hosted-notebook incompatibility. *"This tutorial cannot be run in hosted IPython notebooks like Google Colab or Databricks notebooks. To run the code, you will need to follow the guide to write code on your local device."* — stdio child-process spawn is unsupported in those sandboxes. **First explicit platform-incompatibility statement in the DSPy tutorial corpus**.
- **Quote**: *"In the context of MCP support, DSPy provides a simple interface for interacting with MCP tools, giving you the flexibility to implement any functionality you need."* — closing positioning of DSPy as a thin client over an open tool-source ecosystem.

Constructor name is the only change. This is the **first wiki operational demo of the [[DSPyProgrammingModel|swap-without-modifying-the-signature]] portability claim** between CoT and PoT and the **first concrete printed receipt of the *built-in sound critic* claim** on [[DSPyProgramOfThought]] — both claims were previously documented on the wiki but without a printed before/after.
- **Second headline**: **first wiki receipt of [[LocalSandbox|`dspy.LocalSandbox`]] as a user-facing public primitive.** Prior pages described code execution only as a hidden internal mechanism inside `dspy.ProgramOfThought`; this tutorial walks `sandbox = dspy.LocalSandbox(); sandbox.execute("value = 2*5 + 4\nvalue")` returning `14` **before** introducing the Module — explicitly framing the sandbox as the engine the Module calls into. Two-method surface: `__init__()` and `execute(expr: str)` returning the value of the last expression in `expr`. Mints [[LocalSandbox]] as a new concept page positioned to `dspy.ProgramOfThought` as [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] is to [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] — the thin underlying primitive a wrapper Module orchestrates.

Solves *"square of (atomic number of the metal in the gift from France to the US in the late 19th century) + (sum of digits in the first 10 primes)"* → `'2025'` (= 43² where 43 = 29 + 14). Demonstrates the two-domain payoff: **retrieval for factual lookup, code execution for arithmetic**. Prior multi-hop receipts ([[dspy-rl-multihop-tutorial]], [[dspy-tool-use-tutorial]]) all use `ChainOfThought` or hand-rolled prose reasoning as the answer step.
- **First wiki receipts within this tutorial**: (1) [[LocalSandbox|`dspy.LocalSandbox`]] as a user-instantiable public primitive; (2) `dspy.ProgramOfThought(GenerateAnswer, max_iters=3)` — the iteration-cap kwarg, undisclosed on prior pages (default value still undisclosed); (3) printed CoT-arithmetic-failure-then-PoT-success comparison on the same prompt; (4) `MultiHopSearchWithPoT` composition (`dspy.ChainOfThought` for query generation + `dspy.ProgramOfThought` for final answer); (5) `from dspy.dsp.utils import deduplicate` — first wiki receipt of the legacy `dspy.dsp.*` namespace shim (carried over from the framework's earlier name *Demonstrate-Search-Predict*); (6) [[Llama3|Meta `Llama-3-70b-Instruct`]] in a DSPy tutorial via `dspy.LM("openai/meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-70b-Instruct", api_base="API_BASE", api_key="None")` — first wiki receipt of the placeholder-credentials open-weight pattern (consistent with [[DSPyLM]]'s any-provider posture via [[LiteLLM]]).
- **LM**: Meta `Llama-3-70b-Instruct` via the OpenAI-prefix + LiteLLM-mediated route with placeholder `api_base="API_BASE"` and `api_key="None"` — meant as a fill-in template, not a runnable spec.
- **Retrieval**: `dspy.ColBERTv2(url='http://20.102.90.50:2017/wiki17_abstracts')(query, k=3)` wrapped in plain Python `search_wikipedia(query)` (no `dspy.Tool` wrapper) — same pattern as [[dspy-custom-module]] and consistent with [[ColBERTv2]]'s observation that the wrapper is a retrieval **client**, not a learnable sub-module.
- **Programming stage only**: no metric, no eval set, no [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]]. Sibling to [[dspy-ai-text-game-tutorial]] / [[dspy-sample-code-generation-tutorial]] / [[dspy-custom-module]] in the *show the API surface, not the optimization rung* tier.
- **Cross-receipt against [[DSPyProgrammingModel]]**: the swap-without-modifying-the-signature portability claim becomes operational — same `BasicGenerateAnswer(question -> answer)`, swap `dspy.ChainOfThought(...)` → `dspy.ProgramOfThought(...)`, get a correct answer instead of a wrong one. Prior receipts asserted the swap was possible; this tutorial supplies the printed before/after.
- **Cross-receipt against [[LLMModuloFramework]]**: `dspy.LocalSandbox` is the sound-critic substrate that makes the LLM-Modulo *generate-test-critique* loop operational in DSPy for computable-truth tasks. The Python runtime is a deterministic, sound verifier of arithmetic — exactly the shape Kambhampati et al. argue LLM-prose reasoning is not.
- **Cross-receipt against [[DSPyTools]] / [[DSPyMCP]] / [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]]**: `dspy.LocalSandbox` is structurally the **most permissive** code-execution surface in DSPy — executes arbitrary Python strings, no Signature constraint, no tool inventory, no MCP child-process isolation. The safety boundary is undisclosed by this tutorial (tutorial calls it an *"adapted Python sandbox"* but does not describe what it actually isolates — no file-system / network / process discussion). Open question vs. [[dspy-mcp-tutorial]]'s explicit child-process MCP isolation and [[dspy-tool-use-tutorial]]'s [[func_timeout|`@func_set_timeout(10)`]] + try/except (latter had no isolation beyond timeout).
- **Contradictions flagged**: (1) **`LocalSandbox` safety boundary undisclosed** — the tutorial does not describe what *"adapted Python sandbox"* actually isolates; treat as untrusted-code-adjacent until characterized; (2) the `wiki17_abstracts` [[ColBERTv2]] endpoint at `http://20.102.90.50:2017` is a publicly-hosted shared server with no SLA — operational risk for any reproducer; (3) **no cost / latency / token-budget disclosure** — continuing tutorial-corpus gap; (4) **no `max_iters` ablation** — the kwarg is set to 3 in the multi-hop receipt but the tutorial does not vary it or disclose the default; (5) **two sections labeled `## 3)`** in the source (the ChainOfThought comparison and the Contextual Reasoning section) — upstream copy-paste typo, not a wiki contradiction but a grep-trap for readers; (6) **`api_base="API_BASE"` and `api_key="None"`** are placeholder strings, not runnable values — readers must substitute a real endpoint.

- **Concept page minted**: [[LocalSandbox]] — the user-facing Python-execution primitive `dspy.ProgramOfThought` wraps. Positioned structurally to PoT as [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] is to [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]]. - Source page created: `wiki/sources/mml-ch01-introduction-and-motivation.md` (exhaustive per-chapter ingest of book pp. 11–16 = PDF pp. 17–22; §1.1 Finding Words for Intuitions, §1.2 Two Ways to Read This Book, §1.3 Exercises and Feedback).
- New concept pages created: `Predictor`, `Training`, `FourPillarsOfMachineLearning`.
- Existing concept pages enriched: `MachineLearning` (added data/model/learning trichotomy + predictor/training disambiguation; added source to frontmatter), `Generalization` (added "goal of learning vs. memorization" framing; added source to frontmatter).
- Umbrella `wiki/sources/mml-book.md` updated: added `## Per-Chapter Deep Dives` section with a Ch 1 bullet.
- index.md updated: 1 new Sources entry + 3 new Concepts entries (Four Pillars, Predictor, Training).
- overview.md: no change (Ch 1 is motivational; umbrella already reflects the four-pillars framing).
- Contradictions/quirks: Ch 1 frames training as *maximizing a utility function* (hill-climbing) vs. the wiki's prevailing *minimize loss/cost* framing — same idea up to a sign, noted on the source page and on `Training`. No hard contradictions with `mml-book` umbrella.
- Validation: all introduced [[wikilinks]] resolve to existing pages except `Density estimation` (intentionally NOT created — Ch 1 only previews it; proper home is MML Ch 11; only `KernelDensityEstimation`/`GaussianMixtureModel` exist today). New source page confirmed listed in index.md.

## [2026-06-04] ingest | MML Ch 2 — Linear Algebra
- Source page created: `wiki/sources/mml-ch02-linear-algebra.md` — exhaustive per-chapter deep dive of book pp. 17–69 (= PDF pp. 23–75, offset +6, "2 Linear Algebra" heading verified). Covers §2.1 Systems of Linear Equations, §2.2 Matrices (algebra, inverse, transpose, symmetric), §2.3 Solving Systems (Gaussian elimination, REF/RREF, pivots, particular+homogeneous solution, Minus-1 Trick, inverse via augmented matrix, pseudo-inverse), §2.4 Vector Spaces (groups, GL(n,R), vector-space axioms, subspaces), §2.5 Linear Independence, §2.6 Basis & Rank, §2.7 Linear Mappings (transformation matrices, basis change, image/kernel, rank–nullity), §2.8 Affine Spaces, §2.9 Further Reading. Every Definition (2.1–2.26) and Theorem (2.17, 2.20, 2.24) captured with section + book-page refs; verbatim quotes incl. marginal notes.
- New concept pages created (24): `SystemOfLinearEquations`, `Matrix`, `MatrixInverse`, `IdentityMatrix`, `SymmetricMatrix`, `GroupTheory`, `GeneralLinearGroup`, `VectorSubspace`, `LinearCombination`, `Span`, `Basis`, `Dimension`, `Coordinates`, `RowEchelonForm`, `ReducedRowEchelonForm`, `Pivot`, `TransformationMatrix`, `BasisChange`, `Image`, `NullSpace`, `ColumnSpace`, `RankNullityTheorem`, `AffineSpace`, `AffineSubspace`, `AffineMapping`. (`MatrixMultiplication` already existed — see below.)
- Existing concept pages enriched (10, each with a `## From [[mml-ch02-linear-algebra|MML Ch 2]]` section + source added to frontmatter): `LinearAlgebra`, `VectorSpace`, `LinearMapping`, `LinearIndependence`, `Rank`, `GaussianElimination`, `Determinant`, `MatrixMultiplication`, `MatrixInversion`, `MatrixTranspose`.
- Stub pages resolved: `systemsoflinearequations.md` and `solvinglinearsystemsusinggaussianelimination.md` rewritten to point at the new canonical pages [[SystemOfLinearEquations]] / [[GaussianElimination]]. Disambiguation note added to OS `Kernel.md` pointing to [[NullSpace]].
- Umbrella `wiki/sources/mml-book.md` updated: appended Ch 2 bullet to `## Per-Chapter Deep Dives` (chapter order, after Ch 1).
- index.md updated: 1 new Sources entry (MML Ch 2) + 24 new Concepts entries; gave `Matrix Multiplication` (was bare) a description; added MML refs to `Matrix Transpose`.
- overview.md: no change (umbrella + `LinearAlgebra` concept page already carry the high-level LA framing; this is a per-chapter deep dive).
- Contradictions/quirks: (1) `Kernel.md` = OS kernel, so the LA kernel/null space is filed as [[NullSpace]] (disambiguated both ways). (2) Pre-existing `MatrixMultiplication`/`MatrixInversion`/`GaussianElimination`/`MatrixTranspose` are parallel-computing/Matloff-framed (prime $A'$ notation); kept that perspective and added LA-canonical MML sections. The inverse *object* is [[MatrixInverse]] (MML Def 2.3) vs. the numerical [[MatrixInversion]] page — cross-linked. (3) Transpose notation $\mathbf{A}^\top$ (MML) vs $A'$ (Matloff) — noted. No factual contradictions.
- Validation: grepped all introduced [[wikilinks]]; the only intentional forward-ref is [[OrthonormalBasis]] (MML Ch 3 — not created here; already listed in the umbrella's "concepts introduced" list). All other targets exist (existing pages or the 24 new ones). New source + all 24 new concept pages confirmed in index.md.

- New source page: [[mml-ch10-dimensionality-reduction-pca]] — exhaustive per-section deep dive (§10.1 Problem Setting → §10.8 Further Reading), covering Examples 10.1–10.5, Figs. 10.1–10.16, and Eqs. 10.1–10.81 with §+book-page refs. - The chapter's central result recorded: **three equivalent derivations** (max-variance §10.2, min-reconstruction-error §10.3, latent-variable/PPCA §10.7) all project onto the top-$M$ eigenvectors of the data covariance $\mathbf S=\frac1N\sum_n\mathbf x_n\mathbf x_n^\top$; variance retained $=\sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_m$ (Eq. 10.24); reconstruction error $=\sum_{j=M+1}^D\lambda_j$ (Eq. 10.44).
- New concepts (8 full pages): [[ProbabilisticPCA]] (generative latent model + marginal likelihood + MLE + noise-free limit), [[ReconstructionError]] (the §10.3 objective $J_M$), [[PrincipalSubspace]] (the $M$-dim projection target), [[PowerIteration]] (Eq. 10.52 leading-eigenvector iteration / PageRank), [[DataStandardization]] (the §10.6 per-axis centering+scaling step), [[Whitening]] (the decorrelating generalization), [[FactorAnalysis]] (per-dimension noise relative), [[IndependentComponentAnalysis]] (non-Gaussian-prior relative / blind-source separation). Quoted verbatim: the density-estimation framing (p. 348); "mixture models are more expressive ... multimodal" (p. 349); the "we cannot move the log into the sum over $k$" no-closed-form remark (p. 351–352); the $r_{nk}$ definition + "soft assignment" framing (pp. 352–353); the importance-weighted-Monte-Carlo mean interpretation (p. 354); the Dempster et al. 1977 EM statement + "every step ... increases the log-likelihood" (Neal & Hinton 1999, pp. 360–361); the discrete-vs-continuous-latent contrast with PCA (p. 363); the one-hot/1-of-$K$ statement (p. 364); the responsibility-as-posterior justification (p. 367); the local-optimum / multiple-initialization caveat (p. 367); the MacKay-2003 hard-vs-soft $K$-means statement (p. 368).
- The chapter's central results recorded: the GMM density $\sum_k\pi_k\mathcal N(\boldsymbol\mu_k,\boldsymbol\Sigma_k)$ (Eq. 11.3); responsibilities $r_{nk}$ (Eq. 11.17) = posterior $p(z_k=1\mid\mathbf x_n)$ (Eq. 11.69/11.72b); the three M-step updates — mean $\boldsymbol\mu_k^{\text{new}}=\frac{\sum_n r_{nk}\mathbf x_n}{N_k}$ (Thm 11.1, importance-weighted), covariance $\boldsymbol\Sigma_k^{\text{new}}=\frac1{N_k}\sum_n r_{nk}(\mathbf x_n-\boldsymbol\mu_k)(\mathbf x_n-\boldsymbol\mu_k)^\top$ (Thm 11.2), weight $\pi_k=N_k/N$ (Thm 11.3, via a Lagrange multiplier); EM as alternating E-/M-steps with monotone log-likelihood increase to a local optimum (§11.3); the one-hot-latent generative view + ancestral sampling + marginalized likelihood + expected complete-data log-likelihood $Q$ (§11.4).
- New concepts (3 full pages): [[DensityEstimation]] (the pillar topic; parametric vs nonparametric), [[MixtureWeight]] (the $\pi_k$ / mixing coefficient — convex weight / prior $p(z_k=1)$ / $N_k/N$ update), [[MixtureComponent]] (the per-cluster base distribution; in a GMM a Gaussian, updated by responsibility-weighted MLE).

Three-class lineage on [[GrammarFuzzer|`GrammarFuzzer`]]: `TrackingGrammarCoverageFuzzer` (records `covered_expansions` in `choose_node_expansion`/`add_coverage`), `SimpleGrammarCoverageFuzzer` (prefers `uncovered_children`), and [[GrammarCoverageFuzzer|`GrammarCoverageFuzzer`]] (deep foresight: `new_child_coverage` + breadth-first adaptive `new_coverages` lookahead — Burkhardt 1967 "shortest path selection"). [[ContextCoverage|Coverage in context]] via `duplicate_context()`/`_duplicate_context()` (clones rule subtrees with `new_symbol`/`copy.deepcopy`, prunes `unreachable_nonterminals`). Grammar↔code coverage correlation (≈0.9 CGI, >0.95 URL) measured with [[fuzzingbook-04-coverage|Ch 4]]'s [[Coverage|`Coverage`]] on `cgi_decode`/`urlparse`; bounded by equivalent elements and deep data processing.

## [2026-06-06] ingest | The Fuzzing Book Ch 22 — Mining Function Specifications
- **Source**: *The Fuzzing Book* Ch 22, "Mining Function Specifications" (Zeller, Gopinath, Böhme, Fraser & Holler; CISPA, 2024). `raw/books/fuzzingbook/fuzzingbook-22-dynamic-invariants.md`.
- **Source page**: [[fuzzingbook-22-dynamic-invariants]].
- **Scope**: Daikon-style dynamic specification mining closing Part IV. Traces function calls via `sys.settrace` (`Tracker`/`CallTracker`, capturing `(arguments, return_value)`), then mines two kinds of spec: (1) TYPES — `TypeAnnotator`/`TypeTransformer` read runtime types (`type_string`), rewrite the function AST, and emit PEP 484 annotations (collapsing conflicts to `Any`); (2) value INVARIANTS — `InvariantTracker`/`InvariantAnnotator` check a catalog `INVARIANT_PROPERTIES` of templated properties over metavars `X,Y,Z` (`metavars`, `instantiate_prop`, `prop_function`, `true_property_instantiations`), intersect the satisfied sets across all calls, and emit `@precondition`/`@postcondition` decorators (or inline `assert`s via Exercise 9's `EmbeddedInvariantAnnotator`). Mined specs act as regression oracles; mining overspecializes on few calls and is pruned by diverse runs from a `GrammarFuzzer`. Running examples: `my_sqrt`, `sum2`/`sum3`, `list_length`.
- **New concepts**: [[SpecificationMining]] / [[DynamicInvariant]] / [[InvariantInference]] / [[TypeInference]].
- **Updated concepts**: [[DesignByContract]] / [[Precondition]] / [[Postcondition]] / [[Assertion]] / [[TestOracle]] / [[RunTimeVerification]] / [[DynamicAnalysis]].
- **New entities**: [[Daikon]] (the seminal DAIKON dynamic invariant detector by Michael Ernst et al.; MonkeyType/PyAnnotate mentioned inline, not minted).
